confidence_notes: I ran four web searches. One got the RBA FX observation, which an RBA-domain search summary reported as 0.6720 USD per AUD on 2026-11-18, the latest available. I didn't open the RBA page myself. The other three checked food and drink prices. Beer, coffee and meal anchors come from aggregator sites (Expatistan Jan 2026, Livingcost Oct 2025, Hikersbay, nomad.watch, combien-coute citing Numbeo). These sites disagree: a cappuccino is listed at about USD 2.50-4.70, a pub beer at about CLP 2,800 (roughly USD 3), an inexpensive meal at USD 6-10.5, and a mid-range meal for two at USD 29-57. I used central values. The CLP-to-USD conversions used my own rough rate of about 900-950 CLP per USD, not a searched one, which adds some uncertainty. The cocktail price is based on national pisco sour reports (about CLP 3,500-8,000), shifted lower for Arica. I found no restaurant price for a glass of wine, so wine_glass is set from its usual relationship to beer and cocktail prices in Chile, and it is the least certain drink figure. All four accommodation anchors are my own estimates, without searches or listing checks. They assume a modest hostel market and moderate hotel demand in Arica, so prices may vary with season and with border and tourist traffic.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Arica with other mid-sized cities in northern Chile, mainly Iquique and Antofagasta, and with national Chilean averages. Restaurant and drink prices are set slightly below Santiago. Accommodation is priced like a secondary Chilean coastal city with a small backpacker scene.
